text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

Medieval Italian Princess (and alleged poisoner) LUCREZIA BORGIA, who was the illegitimate daughter of POPE ALEXANDER VI, was born in 1480. She was married three times before she was 18, and is reported to have poisoned all of her husbands.
Australian poet HENRY KENDALL who wrote "Bellbirds" was born in 1839. He was once accused of forging a cheque, but was found 'not guilty' because of insanity.

Australian artist WILLIAM BUSTARD was born in 1894. Known as "Bill the swift", the artist and illustrator created the stainglass window in the Star of the Sea Cathedral in Darwin, which was so well constructed it managed to survive Cyclone Tracey.
British actress HAYLEY MILLS who starred in her first film at age 13, was born in 1946. Among her movies were "Tiger Bay" and "Polyanna".
Australian singer with New World JOHN KANE was born in 1946. Their hits included "Tom Tom Turnaround" (1971) and "Sister Jane" (1972).
West Indian fast bowler MALCOLM MARSHALL, who regularly pulverised English cricket teams, was born in 1958.
** EVENTS **
1775 : American silversmith PAUL REVERE rode from
Charlestown to Lexington, yelling the "British are coming". REVERE was acclaimed as one of the heroes of the American War of Independence.
1831 : Australia's oldest newspaper, the SYDNEY MORNING

HERALD hit the streets for the first time. Originally a weekly paper called the SYDNEY HERALD, it became a daily in 1840, and the word "Morning" was added to the name in 1842. The paper was bought by JOHN FAIRFAX in 1841, and became the basis of the FAIRFAX media empire.
1906 : SAN FRANCISCO was hit by the 'great earthquake',
in which 700 people died, 250,000 were left homeless and 10 square km of the city flattened. While the city has been hit by numerous earthquakes, none has ever created the same amount of devastation.
1909 : 15th century French heroine JOAN of Arc was
beatified at a ceremony at the Vatican.
1923 : Yankee Stadium, home of the New York Yankees
baseball team, was opened.
1934 : The first launderette, the "Washateria", was
opened at Fort Worth, Tex., by J.F. CANTRELL.
1942 : U.S bombers from an American aircraft-carrier
attacked Tokyo for the first time.
1945 : ERNIE PYLE, one of the most famous war
correspondents of World War Two, was killed by Japanese machine-gun fire on the island of Ii Shima in the Pacific. The 1945 film "G.I. Joe" was about his coverage of the Italian campaign.
1946 : The League of Nations dissolved itself and all its
assets were handed over to the United Nations.
1949 : Southern Ireland (Eire) came into being with the
passing of the Republic of Ireland Act.
1951 : Irish-born Australian social worker DAISY BATES

(DAISY O'DWYER HUNT), who worked extensively on the welfare of Aborigines in the North of South Australia, died in Adelaide at the age of 88. She was awarded the C.B.E in 1934, and following the death of her husband (cattleman JOHN BATES) she sold their property and gave the proceeds to Aborigines.
1955 : Renowned scientist and creator of the theory of

relativity, ALBERT EINSTEIN, died in his sleep at the age of 75. Born in Germany, EINSTEIN left his homeland and went to the U-S in 1933, when Hitler became Chancellor. In the US he continued his scientific work, and championed the cause of his Jewish faith. An outspoken pacifist, he nonetheless convinced the American Government to create an Atomic bomb before the Nazis did. However, after the dropping of the first bomb on Hiroshima, he called for the banning of the A-Bomb, which ironically could not have been created without his scientific theories.
1958 : After being detained in a mental asylum for almost

13 years, American poet EZRA POUND was freed. POUND had been charged with treason for making anti-American broadcasts to U.S troops in Italy, but was considered unfit for trial on return to the United States, and sent to a hospital for the criminally insane in Washington D.C.
1966 : The "Sound Of Music" won the Academy Award for
Best Film.
1968 : American oil tycoon ROBERT McCULLOUGH bought
London Bridge for 2 million dollars. The confused American thought he was buying the Tower Bridge.
1979 : US actor LEE MARVIN was ordered by a judge to pay
104,000 dollars in "palimony" to his former lover MICHELLE TRIOLA MARVIN.
1988 : Australia's Secret Intelligence Organisation
(ASIO) reported there were 50 spies in Australia.
1989 : Spanish tenor JOSE CARRERAS gave his first concert
for 3 years, at the Royal Opera House in Covent Garden, following his illness from leukaemia.
1991 : British publisher ROBERT MAXWELL launched his
Mirror Group Newspapers towards a public float, scheduled for the 21st of May.
1996 : Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) gunmen opened
fire on a tourist bus in Cairo, killing 18 Greek tourists.
1996 : More than 100 Lebanese refugees, many of them
women and children, were killed when Israeli artillery shells ripped into a crowded U.N. peacekeepers base where they were sheltering.
1996 : Britain withdrew an expulsion order on Saudi
dissident MOHAMMED al-MASARI, whose presence had threatened lucrative arms deals with Riyadh, and said he could stay in the country for four more years.
